findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than confining it to the VPC. Although the security group currently limits ingress on 3306 to the VPC CIDR, this removes a critical layer of network segmentation and any future or parallel SG rule immediately exposes the production database to the internet.

storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volumes, automated backups, and snapshots, leaving all stored customer data (the EMPLOYEES name/address records) in cleartext on the underlying storage.

The database master password (var.password), username, and endpoint are interpolated directly into the EC2 user_data script. User data is retrievable in cleartext by any process or SSRF-capable web request on the instance via the instance metadata service, and is also visible to any principal holding ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute. Secrets should be retrieved at runtime from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is assumed by an internet-facing web server, so compromise of the PHP application yields full control over all S3 buckets, all EC2 infrastructure (including launching instances and modifying security groups), and all RDS instances in the account — a direct privilege escalation and data exfiltration path.

No metadata_options block is specified, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (optional token). Combined with a web application that takes unvalidated POST input and an instance profile carrying wildcard s3/ec2/rds permissions, a single SSRF or request-forgery flaw lets an attacker read the role's temporary credentials and the plaintext DB password from user data.

The parameter group only sets character set options and does not set require_secure_transport = ON, and the generated PHP client calls mysqli_connect() with no TLS configuration. Database credentials and query results therefore traverse the network unencrypted.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block with encrypted = true is defined, so the instance's root volume — which holds /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc containing the plaintext database password — may be stored unencrypted depending on account defaults.

The database security group allows all protocols to all ports toward 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised database host has an unimpeded outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control; egress from a data tier should be tightly scoped.

The master username is hard-coded to the well-known default "admin", which removes any obscurity from credential-guessing attacks against an instance that is simultaneously marked publicly_accessible.

iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so the only path to the database is the static master password that is already duplicated into EC2 user data and Terraform state. Enabling IAM auth would remove the need to distribute a long-lived shared secret.
